steps.compare: We compare it with what you now pay your rope access contractor: glazed area × number of cleanings × price per m².
steps.share: The robot cleans about 90% of the glazing. Rope access technicians finish corners, canopies and obstructed sections at your price.
steps.crew: The robot needs a crew of two: an operator and a roof safety attendant. We cost their wages, including income tax and social contributions, for every shift.
steps.season: The season runs from mid-April to mid-October. A quarter of the days are lost to rain and wind, and work happens on weekdays. One robot handles about 147,000 m² a year. If the volume is larger, we include a second robot in the calculation.
steps.saving: Savings = what you pay the contractor now − robot cost, brushes and consumables, service at 8% of the price per year, and manual touch-up.
steps.fit: The robot works on continuous glazing. We check the facade’s suitability and roof mounting space during the assessment.

steps.payback: Payback is how many months of savings it takes to cover the purchase. The 5-year net gain is the savings over the service life minus the price of the robots.
steps.lease: Leasing: 20% down payment, 36 months. We show how much you keep each month after the lease payment.

payroll.text: social contributions: since 2026, most companies pay 30%

manual.text: of floor one person cleans by hand per shift

steps.surface: The robot only handles flat hard floors, about 60% of the area in an office. Restrooms, desks and trash stay with people.
steps.freed: We calculate how many full-time positions (FTEs) are freed from floor cleaning, with a margin: 30% of the floor work stays with people.
steps.norm: If you have more cleaners than the norm, each one cleans less, so the same robot frees more FTEs. But never more than half the team.
steps.saving: Savings = wages with contributions + chemicals and water − robot service, consumables and a share of our platform operator’s time.

businessCenter.task: Common-area cleaning relied on a contractor crew: high turnover, quality varied from shift to shift and rates went up every year.
businessCenter.solution: Robotic floor scrubbers clean the lobby and corridors on schedule, with tasks and reports in the platform. People stayed on restrooms and spot jobs.

agro.task: Fields were sprayed with ground machinery: excess product on overlaps, wheel ruts in the crop, and a spraying window that depended on the weather.

construction.task: Manual demolition: a crew with jackhammers, vibration, dust and a risk of collapse next to people. Deadlines slipped for lack of workers.
construction.solution: A remote-controlled demolition robot: the operator works from a safe distance and the machine takes the heavy part of the job.

hero.title: Cleaning robot: how it works and which areas it suits.
hero.lead: A cleaning robot is an autonomous machine: it builds a map of the premises from lidar and cameras, follows a set route, goes around obstacles on its own and returns to its station. It suits large, open areas with level floors. In tight spaces with steps and cluttered floors it often does not pay off.
hero.text: Below, in order: how the robot finds its way, what it does on its own, how much floor it covers on one charge and what to check before buying. The figures come from the datasheet of one model, which we name. Other models differ.

parts.title: What a robot is made of
parts.lead: Four units. Knowing what each one does makes any datasheet easier to read and models easier to compare.

eyes.title: Lidar and cameras
eyes.text: In the Phantas these are a 2D lidar, depth cameras and a color camera, plus anti-drop and anti-collision sensors. The lidar measures the distance to walls and items, the cameras spot obstacles, and the sensors act as a backstop if everything else fails.

brain.title: Map and position
brain.text: From the sensor data the software builds a map and keeps track of where the robot is on it (this is called SLAM). Gausium states a positioning accuracy of ±2 cm using lidar.

tool.title: Brushes, blade, tanks
tool.text: Some robots clean dry (sweeping, vacuuming), some clean wet (a water tank and a squeegee), and some do both. The Phantas scrubs, vacuums, sweeps and dust-mops. Clean-water tank 11.5 L, waste-water tank 10.5 L, dust bag 6 L.

dock.title: Charge and water
dock.text: The station charges the robot and manages the water. The manufacturer adds that it also cleans the squeegee, the suction pipe and the waste-water tank by itself. Without a station, a person does these steps.

nav.title: How the robot finds its way
nav.lead: No floor markings are needed. The robot navigates by a map it built itself. In this it resembles a warehouse AMR, not an AGV, which needs tape or marks.

s1.title: Map
s1.text: The robot drives around the premises and builds a map. Gausium quotes 30 minutes for a 2,000 m² site. Real time depends on the layout and the number of items.

s2.title: Zones
s2.text: In the app the operator edits the map and picks the cleaning zones. A whole floor does not have to be one task.

s3.title: Route
s3.text: The robot plans the path itself: a zigzag or a spiral, as in the Phantas modes. It covers a zone the same way every time, so quality does not depend on who is on shift.

s4.title: Avoiding obstacles
s4.text: While working, the robot checks the map and goes around people and things that are not on it. According to the manufacturer, it avoids cables on the floor but drives over low thresholds.

s5.title: Station and alerts
s5.text: Task done or battery low: back to the station. If there is debris nearby that it cannot pick up, in spot-cleaning mode it sends the operator a message.

area.title: Area one robot covers
area.lead: Two quantities set the area: how much the robot cleans per hour and how long it runs without a recharge. We multiply the Phantas datasheet values.
area.calcAria: 4.5 hours times 350 to 700 square meters per hour equals roughly 1,600 to 3,100 square meters
area.p1: This is our calculation, not a guarantee: output drops with a tight layout and many obstacles. For a larger site, a recharge during the day, a second shift or several robots help. Charging takes about two hours, so plan the schedule in advance.
area.p2: Where this works in practice: offices and office buildings, shopping malls, warehouses, clinics and hotels. Our payback calculator handles sites from 3,500 m², warehouses from 10,000 m². That is the limit of the calculation, not a physical limit of the robot: on a smaller area there is usually too little work for it.

limits.title: When a robot does not fit
limits.lead: Five signs of a site where a cleaning robot most often does not pay off. This is our engineering judgement.

i1.d: A small area or one short shift: the robot sits idle and the savings do not cover the investment.

i2.d: Narrow aisles and frequent turns eat time, and output falls below the datasheet figure.

i3.d: Between floors without an elevator the robot has to be carried, and it does not take high thresholds.

i4.d: Boxes, furniture and pallets in a new place every day: the route breaks and the robot stops.

limits.foot: If your site matches these points, we will say so at the assessment and suggest something else: rental, retrofitting existing equipment, or dropping the project.

check.title: What to check before buying
check.lead: Six questions to answer before signing a contract.

i1.d: Hard floor and carpet are cleaned by different units; in the datasheet they are different modes with different output.

i2.d: Thresholds, elevators, doors that open on their own. One spot where the robot gets stuck breaks the whole route.

i3.d: At night, during a shift or with people around. The number of shifts and the payback period depend on it.

i4.d: You need a power socket and a place to drain water near the working zone.

i5.d: Service and spare parts in Russia, response and recovery times. With us they are fixed in the SLA.

i6.d: Costs with the robot must include service, consumables and operator time, otherwise the period looks attractive and is wrong.

markup.a: No. The robot builds a map of the premises from lidar and cameras and navigates by it. That is why it can be reconfigured when the layout of a hall changes.

people.q: Can the robot run while people are in the room?
people.a: Yes, the manufacturer states that it avoids moving obstacles in real time. Night is still more convenient: fewer people in the way and fewer stops.

staff.a: Not entirely. The robot takes level floor and repeating routes, and staff move to tasks it does not do: restrooms, spot cleaning, quality control. How many people are freed up we calculate at the assessment.

hero.title: Knowledge base: robotics, no marketing.
hero.lead: What clients ask before a deal: how to calculate payback, how an AMR differs from conventional equipment, what robot rental is and when upgrading old equipment pays off better.
hero.text: We write like engineers: the answer first, then figures, timelines and an honest “when it doesn’t pay off”. For an answer about your own site, a site assessment is faster.

payback.q: How fast does a cleaning robot pay back?
payback.a: It depends on three things: how much floor area the robot cleans, how many shifts it works and what cleaner’s wage it replaces. The payback calculator gives an estimate in a couple of minutes. We calculate the exact period during the site assessment and confirm it in a pilot.

cost.q: Too expensive? Can we start without a big outlay?
cost.a: Yes. Robot rental (RaaS) removes the large one-off payment: you pay for use. If you buy, we help with installments and leasing from leading Russian banks. And before any investment, you can run a pilot at your site and check the figures.

breakdown.a: Service is part of the project: maintenance, diagnostics and repairs by our own service network across Russia. Response and recovery times are fixed in the SLA. The platform monitors the fleet, and AI agents predict failures before downtime.

staff.q: Will we have to retrain our staff?
staff.a: Staff training is part of deployment: your people learn to give the robot tasks and work with the platform. Nobody needs retraining. Staff usually move to the work the robot doesn’t do: restrooms, spot cleaning, quality control.

notPaying.a: Sometimes there isn’t enough work for a robot: a small area, one short shift or a task it covers only in part. Then the savings don’t cover the investment. We’ll say so plainly and offer another option: rental, an upgrade of your existing equipment or dropping the project.

amr.q: How do AMRs differ from AGVs?
amr.a: An AGV follows a pre-marked path: magnetic tape or markers on the floor. An AMR (autonomous mobile robot) maps the space itself, plans its route and drives around obstacles. That makes an AMR easier to reconfigure when the warehouse layout changes.

raas.a: RaaS (Robots-as-a-Service) means you pay for using a robot instead of buying it: a lower entry cost and a faster start. You can compare renting and buying on your own figures in the calculator on the Products page.

retrofit.q: Can you automate the equipment we already have?
retrofit.a: Often, yes. Retrofit is an upgrade of existing equipment: we add cameras, navigation, sensors and semi-automatic workflows. It can be faster and cheaper than buying a new robot.

vendors.q: Do you sell robots of a single brand?
vendors.a: No. We are not a manufacturer and are not tied to one brand. For each area we compare 2–5 manufacturers and choose those that fit the task and can be serviced in Russia.
